# Pre-feasibility assessment report, Metis

**Product:** Enterprise Portfolio Intelligence & Governance Platform  
**Source documents:** BRD v4.1 + 35 mid-fidelity wireframes + `manifest.json` + `style-guide.md`  
**Review date:** 2026-10-02  
**Review role:** Business/PMO + Enterprise UX + SaaS/MCP Solution Architecture  
**Review level:** Pre-feasibility, before Discovery/MVP. It does not grade the final aesthetics of the wireframes.

> **Evidence conventions**
>
> - **Observation from the documents**: a conclusion drawn directly from the BRD, the manifest, the digest or the wireframe images. Each remark points to a section, a requirement code or a file name.
> - **Industry knowledge**: benchmarks, heuristics or implementation patterns from outside the documents.
> - **[Needs verification]**: used for market information, competing products, prices, legal matters or outside judgments that must be confirmed in Discovery/procurement/legal review.
> - The data of Acme Holdings, Creative Studio, Digital Products and Project Meridian is fictional sample data. The report checks only **internal consistency**, not real-world correctness.

# 1. Executive summary

## Conclusion: **Conditional Go**

Metis has a product thesis clear enough to invest in a **controlled Discovery**, but not mature enough to be locked as it stands into an MVP build plan. BRD v4.1 did well in merging the POC into a multi-tenant SaaS model, but the P0 scope is now too large: **156 P0**, of which the cross-check against §18.2 shows that Release 1A still carries about **105 P0**, roughly two thirds of all P0. This is not yet a small MVP slice; it is close to a platform foundation plus a complete project execution suite. Evidence: §8 to §11, §18.1 to 18.4.

What most needs protecting is not “having a portfolio dashboard” or “having MCP”. Those groups of capability already exist in many competing products. The thesis of Metis that is worth testing is **one seamless data and governance contract**: the WBS is the single source for the execution surfaces; metrics are computed by the server; lifecycle templates are versioned/pinned; gates/CRs carry evidence and decisions; the LLM goes through the same permission model and only prepares governance decisions for a human to confirm. Evidence: BR-22, BR-32, GOV-19…GOV-26, MCP-05…MCP-16, BR-34…BR-38.

### 5 strengths

1. **A clear single-source execution model.** Charter V/VI, Overview, Timeline, Board, Focus and the report are all derived from the WBS instead of keeping several independent status tables. This directly addresses the POC figure mismatches that the BRD records in §12.2. Evidence: BR-22, WBS-01, §12.1 to 12.2.
2. **Structured and versioned governance.** Lifecycle, gates, mandatory evidence, quorum, waiver, readiness, template provenance and pinning are all described concretely. Evidence: GOV-01…GOV-26, especially GOV-13…GOV-21.
3. **The AI security model is on the right track.** MCP uses the same user permissions, metrics are computed by the server, governance actions are prepare-only, with attribution/audit, token scope/expiry and optimistic versioning. Evidence: MCP-03…MCP-16, BR-34…BR-36.
4. **The BRD has better traceability than a typical POC.** §1 records sources and reconciliation; requirements have acceptance criteria; §12 defines the metrics; §19 openly lists 31 undecided decisions instead of hiding the uncertainty.
5. **The wireframes cover a wide range and the sample data is mostly consistent.** For example Meridian keeps 12 work items, 25% progress and 9 overdue across `24-project-overview.png`, `31-plan-board.png`, `33-journal-reports.png` and `34-focus.png`; the portfolio keeps its main totals across `14-executive-cockpit.png`, `15-workspace-dashboard.png`, `16-portfolio-registry.png` and `18-capacity.png`.

### 5 biggest risks

1. **Scope overload.** 156 P0 and about 105 P0 in 1A make the old 10 to 16 week timeline in §18.4 no longer credible for v4.1; the BRD itself also says it must be re-estimated.
2. **Adoption risk at the PM/team level.** Metis wants PMs to update the WBS, Board, Journal, weekly report, CR and governance; but the two important friction-reducing affordances, quick update and cross-project Focus, are P1/V2 (`OVW-07`, `OVW-08`). This runs against the “PM and team daily execution” journey in §7.9.
3. **The tenant/security architecture still has blocking decisions.** D-20, D-28, D-03 and D-31 are not yet decided while they affect schema, storage, search, cache, backup/restore, auth and procurement.
4. **Concurrency + Builder + multi-surface write is a hard technical combination.** `PLT-05`, `PLT-06`, `WBS-04`, `BLD-03…BLD-07`, `MCP-14` all demand autosave, realtime, conflict detection, rerun safety and idempotency.
5. **Competitive differentiation is not yet proven.** [Needs verification] Planview, Planisware, ServiceNow SPM, Jira Align, Smartsheet, monday.com and Asana all already have many parts of portfolio/work/resource/governance; Asana, monday.com and ServiceNow have also announced MCP capability. “Having MCP” is no longer a moat.

### 5 things to do now

1. **Re-lock Release 1A by 2 to 3 vertical slices**, not by a module list; settle D-01 and build a dependency map for the 156 P0.
2. **Settle the 4 remaining architecture decisions in the top-5:** D-28, D-20, D-03, D-26; run a security/tenancy spike before building broadly.
3. **Bring `OVW-07` and `OVW-08` into the MVP pilot**, or provide an equivalent affordance so PMs can update many projects without jumping between tabs repeatedly.
4. **Prototype the Builder in Discovery, and do not let the Builder block the 1A/1B pilot.** Test 5 to 8 real situations with PMs; keep the manual WBS as the fallback.
5. **Add the missing states/flows to the wireframes before fixing the spec:** create workspace, autosave/conflict, approval queue, notifications, no-permission, quota, stale data and MCP failure states.

# 2. Scorecard

| Item | Score /5 | One-sentence reason |
|---|---:|---|
| A1. Business value | **4** | The internal problem-solution fit is fairly clear, but there is no evidence yet of willingness-to-change or willingness-to-pay. |
| A2. Market and competition | **3** | The SPM/PPM space is crowded and the major capabilities already have competitors; the differentiation thesis must be verified through workflow outcomes, not through feature count. |
| A3. Scope and roadmap | **2** | 156 P0 and about 105 P0 in 1A are still too broad for an MVP with high technical risk. |
| A4. Technical feasibility | **3** | There is no theoretical blocker, but tenant isolation, concurrency, the Builder and MCP authorization need an early spike. |
| A5. Operations and acceptance | **3** | The data model can reduce reconciliation, but PMs must enter a lot of data and the daily work flow is not yet optimized at P0. |
| A6. Commercial feasibility | **3** | There is a reasonable enterprise packaging direction; unit economics still depend on support, compliance, storage/audit and procurement rather than on LLM inference. |
| A7. Legal and compliance | **2** | The BRD identifies the right topics but data residency/compliance target/support access/LLM data boundary are still undecided. |
| B. Wireframe | **3** | Broad and consistent coverage, but many error/state/administrative flows are missing and some screens are very dense. |
| C. User friendliness | **3** | The foundational IA is good; the daily PM flow, approval discovery, Builder accessibility and onboarding need friction to be reduced considerably. |

# 3. Pre-feasibility assessment

## A1. Business value: **4/5**

### Observation from the documents

- **A problem worth solving is described fairly clearly:** project/portfolio data is fragmented; the POC has inconsistent metrics; governance lacks structure; the enterprise needs a portfolio view that can still be traced down to the work item. Evidence: §2 to §5, §12.2.
- **The most important persona for the buying case:** Executive/EPMO/PMO and Workspace Owner. They receive value from `14-executive-cockpit.png`, `16-portfolio-registry.png`, `18-capacity.png`, `19-risk-dependency.png`, `11-lifecycle-framework-designer.png` and `12-gate-review.png`. Evidence: §6, §7.9.
- **The most important persona for adoption:** PM and team. If they do not update the WBS/status/journal, portfolio intelligence loses its reliability. Evidence: §7.9 “PM and team daily execution”; `WBS-01`, `RPT-01`, `OVW-06`.
- **Best fit:** WBS single source + server metric engine + structured governance. This directly fixes the POC failure mode listed in §12.2. Evidence: BR-22, BR-24, BR-32.
- **Weaker fit:** “AI/MCP” by itself does not solve data quality. MCP is only worth anything when the underlying data is already right and permission/audit is enforced. Evidence: MCP-05, MCP-10, MCP-11.

### Industry knowledge

- In enterprise PPM/SPM, an executive dashboard is only valuable if the update cost on the PM/team side is low enough. This is the “garbage in, garbage out” risk; Metis needs to measure **time-to-update** and **freshness** in the pilot instead of only measuring the number of screens built.
- A clear wedge should be chosen for Discovery: **governed execution → trustworthy portfolio roll-up**, instead of selling “PPM + SPM + work management + AI platform” all at once.

### Risks

- The product could become a “system of reporting” that PMs update after doing the real work in Jira/Excel/Teams.
- WBS-first may suit traditional projects/agencies better than some product/agile teams; Q07 and the pilot tenant need to verify it.
- Executives want financial/value data but M19/M20 are P1, while the P0 Cockpit already speaks of investment/value. Evidence: EXE-01…EXE-03, M19, M20.

### Conditions to reach 5/5

- The pilot proves that PMs update the status/weekly report faster or with less duplicate entry than the current process.
- Executive/PMO reach at least one portfolio decision that has traceability from metric → project → WBS.
- Confirm the first 2 to 3 industries/use cases; do not use one common data model to assume that all kinds of projects are alike.

---

## A2. Market and competition: **3/5**

### Observation from the documents

The BRD positions Metis as spanning from project execution to portfolio intelligence and governance (§5, §8). This is the intersection of work management, PPM and SPM; so the competitors are not just one group.

### Industry knowledge: current comparison

> All the information in this table is **[Needs verification]** before an investment decision. The sources checked are the official product pages/documents accessed on 2026-10-02; do not use this table as a market-share study or a procurement comparison.

| Group / product | Public capability close to Metis | Where Metis is only on par | Gap / thesis that could differ |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Planview Portfolios** | [Needs verification] Strategy, investment, capacity, scenario, program/project visibility, outcome/financial planning. | Cockpit, roadmap, capacity, portfolio roll-up are not unusual features. | A WBS-derived execution contract + lifecycle gate evidence + open user-bound MCP could create a different workflow, but this needs to be proven. |
| **Planisware Enterprise** | [Needs verification] Strategic portfolio, roadmaps, budget, scenario optimization, resource capacity/allocation, project execution. | Portfolio/capacity/investment/governance are all areas of direct competition. | Metis could be lighter and more opinionated for governed execution; there is no evidence yet on implementation speed. |
| **ServiceNow SPM** | [Needs verification] Strategy-to-delivery, demand/PPM/resource, workflows, integrations; ServiceNow also has an MCP Server/Client. | Workflow/governance + enterprise integration + AI is not a moat. | “Same metric engine + same permission model + prepare-only governance” must become a clear control model, not just a connector. |
| **Jira Align / Atlassian** | [Needs verification] Strategy-to-team delivery, capacity/investment, dependencies, roadmaps, portfolio/program scale, hybrid frameworks. | Cross-project roadmap/dependency/capacity is a parity zone. | Metis aims at tighter project governance/WBS/charter/gates rather than agile-at-scale; whether it fits depends on the industry. |
| **Smartsheet Portfolios / Control Center** | [Needs verification] Standardized project templates, automated provisioning, portfolio roll-up, resource management, change management. | Template + portfolio roll-up + standardized execution already have a strong benchmark. | Metis could differ in version-pinned governance, gate evidence, WBS-derived multiple surfaces and the MCP policy model. |
| **monday.com** | [Needs verification] Project/portfolio, dependencies, resource/capacity, managed templates, risk insights; has a hosted monday MCP. | Work management + portfolio + MCP is no longer a differentiator. | Metis must win on governance depth, data consistency and executive decision traceability. |
| **Asana** | [Needs verification] Portfolios, goals, workload, approvals, reporting; the official MCP server supports read/write of tasks/projects. | Portfolio visibility, workload, approvals, AI connection are parity at the capability level. | Metis could be stronger in baseline/CR/gate/quorum/waiver and portfolio governance, if the UX is not too heavy. |

**There is no conclusion on price or market share.** The current public pages are not enough to give a credible pricing/market share comparison for a specific use case; therefore the report does not invent numbers.

### Differences that can really be exploited

1. **WBS as canonical execution graph**, every surface derived from the same data (`BR-22`, `WBS-01`, §12). This is an architectural/product discipline, not just a feature.
2. **Version-pinned governance** with mandatory evidence, quorum, waiver, conditions, Decision Log (`GOV-13…GOV-26`).
3. **LLM governance contract:** same permissions (`MCP-05`), server-computed metrics (`MCP-10`), audit attribution (`MCP-11`, BR-34), prepare-only decisions (`MCP-08`, BR-35), optimistic versions/idempotency (`MCP-14`).
4. **No silent rescheduling.** BR-23/WBS dependencies warn but do not change the plan by themselves; this is a control choice suited to governance-heavy organizations.

### What is only on par

- Executive dashboard, portfolio registry, roadmap, resource/capacity, risk view.
- Board, timeline, comments, files, notifications, approvals.
- Configurable templates/workflows at a general level.
- MCP connectivity by itself.
- AI-generated summaries/recommendations by themselves.

### Risks

- Feature breadth causes Metis to be compared with large enterprise suites before it has adoption proof.
- The “single source + governance” difference is hard to see in a sales demo if the UX is slower than the existing tools.
- The MCP ecosystem changes fast; a feature advantage is easily commoditized.

### Conditions to reach 4 to 5/5

- 10 to 15 buyer interviews and 2 design partners confirm that they pay for **governance/data trust** and not just a dashboard.
- A competitive teardown across 5 workflows: project setup, weekly update, gate, CR, executive review; measure the number of steps and the data duplication.
- Choose the first ICP instead of “every enterprise”.

**Sources from outside the documents used for A2, all [Needs verification]:** Planview Portfolios / Strategic Portfolio Management; Planisware Enterprise / Strategic Portfolio; ServiceNow Strategic Portfolio Management; Atlassian Jira Align; Smartsheet Portfolio Management; monday.com portfolio documentation; Asana Portfolios/MCP documentation. The detailed list is in the Appendix.

## A3. Feasibility of scope and roadmap: **2/5**

### Observation from the documents

- Total requirements: **216**, made up of **156 P0, 53 P1, 7 P2**. Counted directly from the requirement tables §9 to §11.
- By the split of §18.2 itself, Release 1A includes about **105 P0**: M01 P0, M02 P0, M03 P0, M05 P0 except MCP-07, M06, M07 except WBS-10/WBS-14, M09, M10, M11, M12 and RSK-01. This is still a large scope.
- 1B has about **51 P0** left, but it holds the hardest items: lifecycle governance, Deliverable Builder/Blueprint, cross-project dependency, portfolio risk, MVP, cockpit/registry/roadmap/capacity.
- §18.4 keeps the old guidance “MVP build 10 to 16 weeks” but states clearly that it must be re-estimated. With v4.1, the old figure should not be used as a commitment.

### Assessment of the current 1A / 1B split

**What is right**
- Moving the Builder to 1B is right; the BRD itself admits that `M08` is “most distinctive” and “hardest”.
- 1A keeps enough WBS/charter/plan/report/CR to prove single-source execution.
- 1A still has the tenant/MCP foundation so as not to create a single-user POC again.

**What is not yet right**
- 1A bundles too much platform breadth at the same time: many auth modes, tenancy lifecycle, export/import, files, notifications, search, PDF, preferences, WBS, board/timeline, report, CR, MCP.
- 1B, for its part, bundles the governance framework + Builder + portfolio control; if it starts sequentially, executive/governance feedback comes too late.
- `OVW-07` quick update and `OVW-08` cross-project Focus are P1 but in reality are adoption enablers for daily usage.

### Scope proposal

Do not redo the architecture. Re-split by **vertical slice**:

**Slice 1: Governed execution pilot**
- Keep: minimal tenant isolation/auth, workspace, project charter core, WBS table/item, Board, Focus, Journal/weekly report, basic CR/baseline, audit, metric engine.
- MCP: read + append journal/comment; one verified client through OAuth/PAT.
- Gate: a fixed/lightly configured lifecycle template can be used in the pilot if the full designer is not ready.

**Slice 2: Configurable governance**
- Versioned lifecycle template, evidence, gate/quorum/waiver, template publish/review.
- MCP prepare-only gate/CR decision.
- A light approval queue.

**Slice 3: Portfolio control**
- Cockpit, registry, capacity, risk/dependency, roadmap based on real data from Slice 1/2.
- The production Builder comes in here only if the prototype proves its value.

### What to cut or defer from the MVP pilot

| Item | Proposal | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `PLT-02` external client access | Defer if the design partner does not need it | Opens up more auth/permission/support surface; D-02 is not yet decided. |
| `PLT-14` import | Keep export, defer the full import | Migration/import creates heavy validation/versioning/error handling; there is no need to prove the core value in the first pilot. |
| `WBS-08` tree diagram | Can be deferred until after the WBS table | Table + item form are enough as the source of truth; the tree is an additional visualization. |
| `GOV-06` advanced conditional flow | Limit the initial rule set | An early rule engine increases the test matrix and the migration/versioning complexity. |
| `M08` Builder production | Prototype in Discovery; do not block the pilot | The risk across UX + canonical model + rerun + accessibility is very high. |
| `M14` MVP module | Feature-flag per workspace | Only needed if the pilot is a product organization; the agency use case does not need it. |
| `RMP-01…RMP-04` full visual roadmap | Keep a lightweight milestone/registry first | The Cockpit/registry can prove the roll-up before the complex visualization is built. |
| Detailed capacity allocation UI | Keep the supply/demand summary; defer the deep editor | The executive value lies in visibility first; an allocation editor increases the data-quality burden. |
| Multi-client MCP guarantee | Publish only a verified compatibility matrix | “Any MCP client” cannot be guaranteed if protocol/auth variations have not been tested. |

### Team and time estimate

**Assumptions**
- Greenfield web SaaS, using managed cloud/IdP/object storage/observability.
- One responsive web app; no native mobile yet.
- 1 to 2 design partners; no ERP/HR/Jira integration P1 in the pilot.
- Reuse component/grid/graph libraries, but do not buy a PPM engine.
- Security review, automated tests and tenant isolation tests are part of the Definition of Done.

**Planning envelope, not a commitment**
- **Discovery + architecture/security/UX validation:** 6 to 8 weeks, 5 to 7 core contributors.
- **Release 1A after reducing scope:** about 5 to 7 months with 10 to 14 FTE.
- **Release 1B / governance + portfolio:** another 4 to 6 months or so with 12 to 16 FTE; part of it can overlap once the foundation is stable.
- **End-to-end to a hardened pilot:** about 9 to 13 months if there are 2 parallel workstreams; a small team working sequentially could take 12 to 18 months.

**Assumed core team:** 1 Product/BA-PMO, 1 delivery lead, 1 UX/product designer, 1 architect/tech lead, 3 to 4 backend/platform engineers, 2 to 3 frontend engineers, 1 QA automation, 0.5 to 1 SRE/platform, 0.5 security/compliance; the Builder may need an additional temporary frontend interaction specialist.

### Conditions to reach 4/5

- A dependency map for the 156 P0 and acceptance tests per slice.
- 1A reduced to one pilot slice that can be demoed end-to-end, not “all foundation + all execution”.
- Do not use the old 10 to 16 weeks as a commercial baseline.

## A4. Technical feasibility: **3/5**

### Observation from the documents

The conceptual architecture in §7.10 is on the right track: one service layer for permission, metric and audit; the tenant boundary covers data/files/search/audit/quotas as well; MCP goes through the same service layer. However the acceptance criteria are not yet enough to guarantee the cross-cutting concerns.

### The five biggest technical risks and how to reduce them

| # | Risk | Evidence | How to reduce |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Cross-tenant data leak** through the DB, search, cache, files, queue, export or support tooling | `TEN-02`, BR-33, §17 Multi-tenancy, D-28 | Tenant context mandatory on every request/job; DB policy/RLS or equivalent; tenant-scoped object keys/search indexes/cache keys; automated negative tests; support grants with an expiry; restore drills per tenant. |
| 2 | **Lost update / conflict** between browser users and MCP writes | `PLT-05`, `PLT-06`, `MCP-14`, `WBS-04` | Record version/ETag; optimistic concurrency; idempotency key; event stream for refresh; conflict UI showing the server value + local change; no silent “last write wins”. |
| 3 | **The Deliverable Builder becomes a mini modeling product that is hard to stabilize** | `BLD-01…BLD-10`, §18.3 | Separate the canonical process graph from the canvas layout; use a proven graph library; deterministic build/rerun; versioned schema; a single active canvas editor in the pilot; a list/form fallback with keyboard support. |
| 4 | **MCP compatibility + auth/safety** differ between clients | `MCP-01…MCP-16`, D-29, Q08 | Conformance tests against the 2026-07-28 spec; compatibility matrix; a clear OAuth + PAT profile; same policy engine as UI; scope minimization; rate limit; audit; prepare-only high-risk actions; verified clients before claiming “any”. |
| 5 | **Derived metrics/report/PDF not on the same snapshot** leading to mismatched figures | BR-22, BR-32, `PLT-16`, `RPT-03`, §12 | A single metric service; snapshot/version ID when generating the report/PDF; async tenant-scoped job; regression fixtures; the PDF states “data as of” and the source version. |

### MCP server

- **On the right track:** the BRD uses Streamable HTTP, OAuth/PAT, scopes, audit and user permissions (`MCP-01…MCP-05`). The MCP 2026-07-28 spec in practice moves the core to stateless request/response, adds routing headers and authorization hardening; a stateless architecture will suit the gateway/rate limiting better.
- **The claim needs fixing:** §7.10 says “LLM clients (any MCP-capable application)”. In practice clients differ in protocol revision, OAuth/DCR behavior and supported transport. It should be changed to **“standards-compliant MCP clients; verified clients listed in compatibility matrix”**. Internal evidence: Q08 is not yet closed.
- **A good safety contract:** `MCP-08` prepare-only governance + BR-35 require that governance decisions be confirmed by a person in the app. This should not be loosened in the MVP.
- **To be added:** action classification: read, low-risk write, reversible write, governance/high-risk. Each class has a different confirmation/undo/idempotency policy.

### Multi-tenant isolation

D-28 must be settled before the schema. At a minimum there must be a threat model for: SQL/ORM, search, object storage, async queue, cache, metrics, audit export, support console, backup/restore and observability. `TEN-02` says “every data path”, but the acceptance test is for now only a statement of principle.

### Canvas + many people editing

A realtime collaborative canvas should not be built right away. `PLT-06` applying to the whole project does not mean the Builder needs multi-cursor/OT/CRDT. Let 1 editor hold a short lease on the canvas in the pilot; other users are read-only + “request edit”. The WBS table still uses optimistic concurrency.

### PDF generation

`PLT-16` requires the PDF to equal the on-screen content at the time of export. “At export time” needs to be defined by an immutable snapshot/version, because async generation may run after the data has changed. Testing is needed for fonts, locale, page breaks, charts/table alternatives, large WBS and tenant branding when P1 is switched on.

### Integrations

Having only SSO/MCP/email at P0 (§16) is reasonable. The P1 ERP/HR/Jira/ADO/chat/cloud storage/DWH integrations should go through an adapter contract + webhook/job idempotency, and integration-specific fields must not leak into the canonical WBS/governance schema.

### Conditions to reach 4/5

- Architecture Decision Record for D-28/D-20/D-03.
- Working spikes: tenant isolation negative tests, 2-user WBS conflict, one MCP OAuth client + PAT client, Builder canonical graph/rerun, deterministic PDF snapshot.
- Threat model + abuse cases for MCP and support access.

## A5. Operational feasibility and level of acceptance: **3/5**

### Observation from the documents

- The PM must set up the charter/WBS, update the Board/WBS, Journal, weekly report, CR and gate evidence (§7.9).
- `OVW-07` quick update and `OVW-08` cross-project Focus are nonetheless P1. `34-focus.png` therefore does not yet serve well someone who manages many projects.
- `PLT-09` notifications is P0 but there is no wireframe yet for the notification center/preferences.
- Workspace setup needs create/profile, fields, team, lifecycle, process frameworks (§7.9), but the wireframes only show depth from fields/team/framework onwards; the create/profile flow is missing.

### Industry knowledge

A PM will not enter the same status into two systems for long. If Metis is not the only execution system, the product must have import/sync or create enough value for PMs to switch their workflow completely. Because the P1 integrations come later, the pilot should choose a team that is ready to use Metis as the system of record.

### Operational risks

- Data freshness drops if the weekly update is a “reporting chore”.
- The tenant admin is overloaded when they have to configure fields/roles/frameworks by themselves from a blank state.
- Template proliferation if each workspace clones and then edits without an owner/deprecation policy.
- Role/approval changes can leave a project stuck if the approver leaves the organization.

### Proposals

1. Raise `OVW-07/08` into the pilot or add an inline status update in the global Focus.
2. Onboarding wizard: tenant security → workspace profile → starter template → team/roles → first project.
3. A “Configuration readiness check” before publishing the lifecycle: missing approver, orphan role, invalid transition, unresolved option mapping.
4. A data freshness badge on portfolio cards; owner + last updated + source.
5. Adoption metrics: weekly active PMs, % active projects updated on the right cadence, median time to weekly update, % metrics computed without needing a manual override, stale-project rate.

### Conditions to reach 4/5

- A 4 to 6 week pilot proves that PMs use Focus/Board/Journal as a work surface, not only re-entering data at the end of the week.
- Starter templates are enough for the first workspace to work within one guided configuration session.
- There is an owner for template/configuration governance.

## A6. Commercial feasibility: **3/5**

### Observation from the documents

- `TEN-05`, `TEN-10`, `TEN-14`, BR-38 already have plan/limits/fair-use concepts.
- The customer uses their own LLM through MCP; **Metis does not pay the model inference fee for this MCP use case** according to the product context. Even so, Metis still bears the cost of serving the MCP endpoint, audit, storage, rate limiting, support and data egress.
- Billing/self-serve metering is P1; this suits an enterprise-first pilot.

### Pricing model hypothesis

No price figure is given.

- **Base platform/tenant fee:** tenancy, security, audit, core project execution.
- **Seat/role bands:** paid internal users; guest/client access can be included or priced lower.
- **Module/tier packaging:** advanced governance + portfolio/capacity/analytics instead of unlocking each micro-feature.
- **Usage guardrails:** storage, report/PDF jobs, audit retention, MCP request volume; avoid pure per-MCP-call pricing because it may make customers reluctant to use automation.
- **Enterprise options:** dedicated residency/region, enhanced support, SCIM, custom retention, premium implementation. MFA/audit/basic SSO security should not be turned into a “luxury add-on” if the target is the enterprise.
- BR-38 must win over commercial logic: exceeding a limit must not block customers from reading/exporting their own data.

### Main cost factors

Cloud DB/storage/search/cache, audit retention, PDF workers, notifications/email, observability, backups/restore, security testing, SSO/SCIM support, tenant onboarding/support, certification/compliance program, data residency/dedicated environments and implementation services.

### Risks

- Enterprise onboarding/support cost may be higher than the software margin if the configuration is too flexible.
- If each tenant needs custom framework consulting, Metis turns into a services-heavy PPM implementation.
- MCP has no model cost but has a support cost because of client compatibility.

### Conditions to reach 4/5

- Discovery has a packaging hypothesis and 3 to 5 procurement interviews.
- The template/config setup time is measured.
- Define clearly which part is product configuration and which part is paid implementation.

---

## A7. Legal and compliance: **2/5**

### Observation from the documents

The BRD has named data residency (D-20), security/compliance target (D-31), support access grants (`TEN-09`, BR-37), export/offboarding (`TEN-07`), audit (`PLT-11`), tenant isolation (`TEN-02`) and SOC 2/ISO 27001 as targets in §17. These are the right topics but not yet a complete compliance design.

### Industry knowledge

- **[Needs verification]** Legal obligations depend on where the customer/users are located, the type of data, the controller/processor role and the contract. Discovery needs legal counsel to determine the DPA, cross-border transfer, retention/deletion, subprocessor disclosure, breach response and data subject obligations where applicable.
- SOC 2/ISO 27001 are assurance/certification programs and do not replace specific privacy/residency requirements.
- When a user connects an external LLM through MCP, the data may leave the Metis security boundary for a provider chosen by the customer. “Customer pays LLM” does not mean “Metis has no governance responsibility any more”.

### Mandatory additions before the spec freeze

1. Data classification: project metadata, files, comments, audit, identity, secrets/tokens.
2. Retention matrix: active, archived, deleted, audit, backups, support logs.
3. Region/residency behavior: DB, object storage, search, backup, telemetry.
4. Subprocessor inventory and tenant-facing notice. [Needs verification]
5. Support access break-glass: reason, approver, expiry, recording, customer-visible log.
6. MCP data egress policy: tenant admin allow/deny, scopes, workspace restrictions, sensitive field/tool redaction, token rotation/revoke.
7. Secret handling: PAT hash-at-rest; OAuth secrets/refresh tokens encrypted; no secret in audit payload.
8. Offboarding test: full export + deletion/retention evidence.

### Conditions to reach 4/5

- D-20 and D-31 closed with the legal/security stakeholders.
- Security control matrix + threat model + incident response + vendor/subprocessor review.
- Prove tenant restore/delete/export and MCP egress controls in the pilot.

---

## A8. Conclusion

### Decision: **Conditional Go**

**Preconditions for moving from Discovery to a committed MVP build**
1. Re-scope 1A into a pilot vertical slice and update §18.
2. Settle tenant isolation + hosting/residency + auth architecture.
3. Prototype concurrency and the Builder before locking the estimate.
4. Bring the daily PM adoption flow into P0.
5. Have 1 to 2 design partners and quantitative success metrics for data freshness, update effort and decision traceability.
6. An MCP compatibility matrix; do not claim universal client support before testing.
7. Supplement the wireframes with the important state/error/permission/approval/onboarding screens.

### The 5 decisions in §19 that must be settled first

| Decision | Why it must be settled early |
|---|---|
| **D-01: Scope sequencing** | It decides every estimate, staffing, pilot acceptance and dependency. If it is not settled, every timeline is just a feature inventory. |
| **D-28: Tenant isolation model** | It is a blocking architecture matter for the DB, files, search, cache, async jobs, support access and restore. A mistake here is very hard to retrofit. |
| **D-20: Cloud, regions, residency** | It affects infrastructure, the storage/search/backup topology, procurement and compliance. |
| **D-03: Authentication methods** | SAML/OIDC/password/MFA/magic-link/external access decide the IdP strategy and the account model; many flows should not be built in parallel before the pilot is known. |
| **D-26: Measurable NFR targets** | Without concurrency, latency, availability, RPO/RTO and scale targets, neither the architecture nor the Definition of Done can be assessed. |

**The group of decisions right after the top-5:** D-29 MCP auth, D-24 metric definitions, D-02 client access, D-31 compliance target, D-09 Builder semantics.

# 4. Wireframe assessment

## B1. Coverage

### Observation from the documents

`manifest.json` maps 35 screens to requirement IDs. Cross-checking all the P0 requirements in the BRD shows that **22 P0 are not mapped to any screen in the manifest**. Not all 22 need a screen of their own; but they create three different kinds of gap.

### 22 P0 not yet mapped in the manifest

| Requirement | Kind of gap | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| `PLT-05` Server persistence/autosave | **Missing UX state** | Needs saving/saved/failed/retry on the main editors, especially `25-project-charter.png`, `26-wbs-table.png`, `28-wbs-item.png`, `29-deliverable-builder.png`. |
| `PLT-06` Concurrent editing | **Serious missing UX state** | There is no presence, stale version, conflict dialog or merge/reload pattern yet. |
| `PLT-07` File storage | Traceability + error state | File attachments appear in the item/activity, but the manifest does not map them; the oversized/blocked/malware/upload failed states are missing. |
| `PLT-08` Docs & Links | **Missing surface** | The project navigation has the requirement but there is no Docs & Links screen yet. |
| `PLT-09` Notifications | **Missing surface/state** | There is no inbox, notification preferences, approval request state or unread indicator. |
| `PLT-12` Search | **Missing result flow** | The top search chrome is present but there is no result/empty/no-permission state. |
| `PLT-14` Export/import | **Missing flow** | Some screens have an export/PDF affordance, but there is no JSON export/import-new-project journey, validation or failure report yet. |
| `PLT-15` Protected destructive actions | **Missing state/flow** | There is no typed confirmation, retention/restore view or deleted-project state yet. |
| `PLT-16` Document generation | Traceability gap | Export/PDF exists in `25-project-charter.png` and `33-journal-reports.png`; the manifest should map `PLT-16`. |
| `PLT-18` Personal preferences | **Missing surface** | There is no default landing tab/WBS view preference yet. |
| `TEN-02` Absolute tenant isolation | Backend/security | No screen of its own is needed, but a 403/cross-tenant negative state and test evidence are needed. |
| `WSP-01` Create workspace | **Missing flow** | The journey in §7.9 starts with creating a workspace but the wireframes start from settings that already exist. |
| `WSP-02` Workspace isolation | Backend/security | No screen of its own is needed; an unauthorized state and server tests are needed. |
| `WSP-03` Workspace profile/calendar/cadence | **Missing surface** | There is no General/Profile screen even though the setup journey needs one. |
| `WSP-04` Workspace switcher | Traceability + state | The switcher is seen in the shell but the manifest does not map it; the loading/preserve-context/no-access-after-switch states are missing. |
| `WSP-05` Workspace lifecycle | **Missing flow** | There is no archive/suspend/restore/read-only state for the workspace yet. |
| `WSP-06` Workspace navigation tree management | **Missing admin flow** | The sidebar shows the tree but there is no create/rename/move/archive management yet. |
| `MCP-07` Update tools | **Missing AI-write state** | There is no UI that distinguishes a change made by MCP, a conflict, undo/review or a policy for low-risk writes. |
| `MCP-09` Stable/versioned tool contracts | Backend/API | No screen of its own is needed; version/compatibility must be surfaced in the AI Access docs. |
| `MCP-13` Data minimization | Backend/policy | No screen of its own is needed; there should be an admin scope/tool policy explanation. |
| `MCP-14` Idempotency + optimistic record versions | Backend + conflict UX | Needs an error/retry/conflict state in `08-profile-ai-access.png`/activity and on the affected record. |
| `MCP-16` Prompt-injection safety | Backend + admin education | There is no policy explanation, safe-tool boundary or security troubleshooting yet. |

In addition, **`MCP-10` is P0 but the manifest only maps it to `23-ai-copilot.png` (V3)**. This requirement is in fact server-computed metrics for MCP and needs to be shown in the MVP AI Access/connection docs rather than depend on the V3 Copilot.

### Important screens/states still missing

1. Workspace create + General/Profile + archive/suspend.
2. Project create flow and lifecycle/template choice; `PM project setup` in §7.9 starts with creating a project but there is no corresponding screen.
3. A light global **Approvals / Requests** queue for gate/CR; the `EXE-04` Decision Center is V2, while approval is P0.
4. Notification center/preferences.
5. Search results.
6. Docs & Links.
7. Autosave/conflict/recovery.
8. Plan/quota reached; payment/billing is not needed at P0 but the behavior when a limit is hit must exist.
9. No permission / access revoked / session expired.
10. Stale data / partial aggregation / integration delayed.
11. Import validation/errors.
12. MCP expired token / insufficient scope / rate limit / unsupported client / conflict.
13. Empty states for new tenant/new workspace/no project/no WBS/no capacity data.
14. Delete + retention + restore.

## B2. Information architecture and navigation

### Sidebar and workspace switching

**Observation from the documents**
- The shell is consistent across screens; the Workspace/Portfolio/Project context is easy to recognize visually.
- `WSP-04` requires switching workspace while keeping the context but there is no detailed flow/state yet.
- The admin screens `02` to `07` use a navigation of their own, which is reasonable for the tenant/provider scope.

**Problems**
- A user may not know whether they are in **tenant-level admin**, **workspace-level settings** or **project-level execution** if relying only on the sidebar label.
- The workspace tree has no management affordance yet (`WSP-06`).
- No behavior is seen for when the same project name appears in several workspaces or when a user loses permission after a switch.

**Proposals**
- Always show a breadcrumb/context chip: `Tenant / Workspace / Project`.
- The workspace switcher shows the current tenant + workspace, recent workspaces, search, a permission badge.
- Preserve the current project only if the project exists and the user has permission; if not, go to the workspace home with a clear message.

### The project tabs: Overview, Charter, WBS, Plan, Governance, Focus

**What is good:** The style guide and the images keep the same order. The mental model from summary → source data → plan → governance → personal work is relatively easy to learn.

**Problems**
- `Governance` could cover CR/gate/decision but the screen coverage is mainly separate gate/CR screens; a landing page is missing for the user to know the overall governance status.
- `Focus` at the project level makes a multi-project user switch repeatedly; the cross-project `OVW-08` is V2 though.
- Docs & Links (`PLT-08`) is said to open from the project node but it is unclear whether it sits in a tab or in the tree, so it is easily split from the mental model.

**Proposals**
- Keep 6 tabs, do not add many new tabs.
- Give `Governance` a minimal landing page: current stage/gate, open CRs, decisions, waivers.
- A global Focus in the workspace shell; the project Focus stays contextual.
- Docs & Links opens from the project secondary navigation but the breadcrumb still keeps the project context.

### The location of Approvals and the admin screens

**The big problem:** the P0 approval actions are scattered across `12-gate-review.png` and `32-change-requests.png`; the CEO journey in §7.9 on the other hand speaks of “recommended decisions”; the `EXE-04` Decision Center is V2. There is no single P0 place for “what is waiting for my approval”.

**Proposals**
- Do not pull the full V2 Decision Center into the MVP.
- Add a small **My approvals** queue in the shell/notifications: type, project, requested by, due, blocker, deep-link to the gate/CR.
- Keep the tenant admin and workspace settings separate; do not mix governance approval into the admin console.

### The path from the portfolio down to the project

`14-executive-cockpit.png` → attention item → project/gate/CR and `16-portfolio-registry.png` → project are good drill-down paths. `17-roadmap.png`, `18-capacity.png`, `19-risk-dependency.png` must also use the same deep-link contract: clicking a project/WBS item opens the right context and has a **Back to filtered portfolio** that keeps the filter/sort/time period.

---

## B3. Consistency

### Terminology

- **Category vs Type:** `09-workspace-fields-options.png` already tries to distinguish them, but newcomers still easily confuse them. Evidence: `WSP-07…WSP-09`, BR-24.
- **Stage vs Phase:** the lifecycle uses “Stage”; the workspace/WBS has “Phase”. A glossary is needed and the two words must not be used interchangeably.
- **Baseline, gate, waiver, Focus:** are domain terms and need in-context help; see C4.
- **Approver/Reviewer/PIC:** fairly consistent across Charter/WBS/Gate, but role inheritance/override must show its source.

### Components, color and shape state

- The style guide requires state to always have **color + shape + text**; RAG uses `● On track`, `▲ At risk`, `■ Off track`. This is a good pattern.
- The images generally keep a light border, a violet accent and a consistent chip pattern.
- The heatmap/chart in `18-capacity.png` has a table alternative per the style rule; it must be ensured that the implementation keeps this.
- Some V2/V3 actions are stuffed into the MVP wireframes as disabled/labeled items. This is useful for the roadmap discussion but is easily read as “the MVP has it ready”; a standard visual treatment is needed for future capability.

### Consistency of the sample data

**Matches well**
- Meridian: **12 work items / 25% / 9 overdue** match across `24-project-overview.png`, `31-plan-board.png`, `33-journal-reports.png`, `34-focus.png`.
- The Charter has 3 deliverables, matching the Overview. `25-project-charter.png`, `24-project-overview.png`.
- The Digital Products portfolio keeps its main totals `$50.2M`, 128 projects and the demand/capacity context across `14`, `15`, `16`, `18`.

**Needs fixing**
1. `27-wbs-tree.png` describes the dependency `1.2 → 3.2` as type FS and says there is a conflict, but the digest shows that the successor `3.2` has no start date yet in the WBS. According to `WBS-13`, an FS conflict needs the predecessor's finish compared with the successor's start. If the start is missing, there is not enough data to assert a conflict. **Fix the sample date or the rule/annotation.**
2. `12-gate-review.png` has quorum/vote count wording that is easily read as two different denominators. A consistent format is needed: `1/3 votes · quorum 2/3`, for example.
3. `14-executive-cockpit.png` says “6 items need a decision” but the attention list mixes decision, reminder, rebalance and review. Change it to “6 items need attention”; decision is a subtype.

---

## B4. Missing states

| State | Related screens | Risk if missing | Proposal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Empty/new tenant | `07`, `14` to `19` | An empty dashboard does not tell the user what to do | Starter checklist + create workspace/project CTA. |
| Loading/partial | `14` to `19`, `24` | A slow aggregation is easily read as 0 | Skeleton + “last refreshed” + partial data warning. |
| Error/retry | whole app | An enterprise workflow cannot rely on a generic toast alone | Inline error per component; retry; correlation ID for support. |
| No permission | `12`, `16`, `25` to `35` | The user sees a link but does not know why they cannot get in | A 403 state naming the resource + role + request-access route. |
| Access revoked mid-session | editor screens | A save could fail/overwrite | Freeze editor, preserve local draft, explain re-auth/request access. |
| Autosave failed | `25`, `26`, `28`, `29`, `32`, `33` | Data loss | Persistent save indicator + retry/download draft. |
| Concurrent conflict | `26`, `28`, `32`, MCP write | Silent overwrite | Version conflict panel + compare/reload/reapply. |
| Plan/quota limit | `02`, `05`, file/MCP | The user is blocked suddenly | Pre-limit warning + admin link; BR-38 keeps read/export. |
| Stale data | `14` to `19` | The executive makes a decision from old data | Freshness timestamp/badge per source/project. |
| File rejected/scanning | `28`, Docs & Links | Security/upload confusion | Scanning, blocked type, oversize, malware states. |
| Tenant/workspace suspended | `01`, `07`, shell | Ambiguous login/error | Read-only/suspended screen + admin contact + export if policy allows. |
| MCP token expired/revoked | `08` | LLM client “mysteriously” fails | Connection status + last error + rotate/reconnect. |
| MCP insufficient scope | `08`, affected record | Hard for the user to debug | Exact missing scope/workspace + no secret leakage. |
| MCP rate-limited | `04`, `05`, `08` | Retry storm | Retry-after guidance + usage panel. |
| Unsupported MCP client/revision | `08` | “Any client” promise breaks | Compatibility diagnostic + verified client list. |
| Baseline locked | `25` to `32` | The user does not understand why a field is disabled | The existing CR banner pattern extended to a field-level explanation. |
| Archived/deleted project | registry/project | Dead links | Tombstone + restore window/owner. |

---

## B5. Accessibility

### Observation from the style guide and the wireframes

- The style guide already requires **not relying on color alone**, using shape + text for RAG; this is a good point.
- `#6C6C78` is recorded as 5.2:1; `#A0A0AC` 2.6:1 is only for placeholder/disabled. The implementation must prevent the use of the faint color for real information.
- Dense table 13px, secondary 12.5px and section label 11px all-caps make the screens `12`, `18`, `19`, `25`, `26`, `28`, `29`, `33` highly dense.
- BRD §17 says keyboard alternative for the canvas “where feasible”. For the Builder/WBS tree, this is not specific enough.

### Risks and proposals

1. **Builder canvas (`29-deliverable-builder.png`):** every node/edge/action must have an equivalent list/form editor, a keyboard focus order, add/connect/delete through a command/menu; not drag alone.
2. **WBS tree (`27-wbs-tree.png`):** tree semantics, expand/collapse by keyboard, visible focus, announce the hierarchy level.
3. **Board (`31-plan-board.png`):** dragging a card must have a Move to status action by menu/keyboard.
4. **WBS table (`26-wbs-table.png`):** grid keyboard pattern, a frozen column that does not break focus, column chooser, 200% zoom without losing actions.
5. **Gate/CR forms:** a validation message attached to the field, a summary at the top, not just a red outline.
6. **Charts/heatmaps:** direct labels or a table equivalent; keep the style guide rule.
7. **Typography:** 11px labels are used only for secondary metadata; body/interactive text does not drop to this level.
8. **Motion/hover:** do not let information appear only on hover.
9. **Touch/mobile:** 36px dense rows may be cramped for touch; responsive mobile should switch to cards/detail, not force the full WBS grid.
10. **Focus visibility:** add a separate token for keyboard focus, and do not use the selected violet for the focus state as well.

### Conclusion B

The wireframes reach a level that is **enough for Discovery usability testing**, not yet enough to freeze the implementation spec. The biggest gap is not aesthetics but **state completeness, daily workflow and the accessibility contract**.

# 5. Level of user friendliness

## C1. Walking through the 10 journeys in §7.9

**How operations are counted:** this is an estimate from static wireframes. An “operation” is a page/tab transition or a main click/decision; individual typed characters are not counted and no shortcut that has not been designed is assumed. The range of operations is used to compare relative friction, not as a measured usability benchmark.

| Journey §7.9 | Path through the existing screens | Estimated operations | Friction point | Proposed shortening |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| **1. CEO weekly review** | `14-executive-cockpit.png` → attention item → `12-gate-review.png` / `32-change-requests.png` / project detail → decision log | **5 to 9** for one item | The journey says “recommended decisions” and publishing the Decision Log, but the `EXE-04` Decision Center is V2; the attention list also mixes decisions with reminder/rebalance. | The Cockpit uses Action type; add My approvals at P0; the decision deep-link opens the right evidence and after confirming writes to the log by itself, without making the CEO navigate to the log. |
| **2. Product Director portfolio review** | `14`/`15` → `17-portfolio-roadmap.png` → `35-mvp-detail.png` → `18-capacity.png` / `19-risk-dependency.png` → `21-scenario-planner.png` (V2) | **8 to 14** | The journey's “create a scenario” step depends on a V2 screen. The MVP does not complete the journey as described. | In P0 give a lightweight “compare current options” or fix §7.9 to state clearly that scenario is V2; preserve filters when jumping between roadmap/capacity/risk. |
| **3. PM project setup** | **The Create project screen is missing** → `25-project-charter.png` → `29-deliverable-builder.png` or `26-wbs-table.png` → `28-wbs-item.png` assignments → `12-gate-review.png` | **20 to 40+** plus data entry | The create project/lifecycle choice has no wireframe; the Charter is long; the Builder is complex; the gate has a lot of evidence. | A setup wizard: Basics → lifecycle/template → charter essentials → WBS → roles → readiness. Allow save-and-exit; derived Charter sections do not make people re-enter data. |
| **4. PM & team daily execution** | `34-focus.png` → `28-wbs-item.png` or `31-plan-board.png` → comment/activity → `33-journal-reports.png` | **6 to 12/project** | Focus is project-level only; quick update `OVW-07` and cross-project `OVW-08` are V2, forcing people with many projects to change context. | Global Focus + inline status/comment; a one-click “Log to Journal” from the WBS/Board; bring OVW-07/08 into the pilot. |
| **5. PM weekly update** | `24-project-overview.png` → `33-journal-reports.png` Build → declared health/narrative → publish; if the baseline changes → `32-change-requests.png` | **8 to 13** | The Report Builder and Journal/Saved are easily confused if the UI is not truly tabbed; the metric snapshot/freshness is not prominent. | Pre-fill computed metrics + changes since the last report; the PM writes only the narrative/exceptions; publish has a preview + snapshot ID. |
| **6. Change request** | `32-change-requests.png` log CR → affected items/impact → approver decision → PM Apply → new baseline | **9 to 15** across 2 roles | Requester/approver/apply actions live on the same screen; “Approved” is easily confused with “Applied”. | Role-specific action bar; a clear state machine Draft→In review→Approved→Applied; diff before apply; notification deep-link. |
| **7. Gate review** | Stage owner evidence → `12-gate-review.png` readiness → approvers → rationale/conditions → Decision Log | **8 to 14** | A very dense screen; if mandatory evidence is missing while the decision control is still active it creates an error-prevention risk. | Sticky eligibility summary; blocker list click-to-fix; invalid decision disabled + reason; conditions automatically create a tracked action. |
| **8. Tenant onboarding** | `07-provider-tenants.png` create tenant → invite first admin → `03-tenant-admin-security.png` → `02-tenant-admin-users.png` → **create workspace screen missing** → workspace settings | **15 to 30+** | The region/auth choice is not yet settled; create workspace/profile is missing; the admin has to jump across many settings pages. | Onboarding checklist/wizard; test SSO before enforcing; starter workspace template; resume progress. |
| **9. Connect LLM through MCP** | `08-profile-ai-access.png` → OAuth connect **or** create PAT → copy endpoint/config → external client → test/activity/audit | **5 to 8 OAuth**, **7 to 10 PAT**, not counting client-specific setup | Client behavior differs; “any MCP client” is too broad; scope/token/rate errors have no design yet. | Verified-client presets + generic manual config; connection diagnostics; copy-safe config; last successful call + audit deep-link. |
| **10. Workspace setup** | **create/profile missing** → `09-workspace-fields-options.png` → `10-workspace-team-roles.png` → `11-lifecycle-framework-designer.png` → `13-template-library.png` | **25 to 50+** depending on the framework | Blank-canvas configuration is too heavy; the lifecycle/process terminology is hard; publish validation is not clear enough. | Starter templates, setup wizard, readiness checklist, validation errors per section, preview a sample project before publish. |

### Concluding points from the 10 journeys

- **The two executive journeys do not fully match the phases:** the CEO depends on the notion of “recommended decisions”; the Product Director depends on the V2 Scenario Planner.
- **The two setup journeys lack a starting point:** project create and workspace create/profile.
- **The most important adoption journey is phased the wrong way round:** the PM daily flow needs `OVW-07/08`, but they are P1/V2.
- **The MCP journey has the best UX among the admin flows** thanks to `08-profile-ai-access.png`, but the reliability states are not enough.
- **Gate/CR has good domain fidelity**, but the density and the role/action state need simplification.

Severity scale: **0** not a problem; **1** cosmetic; **2** minor; **3** major; **4** usability catastrophe / could cause a wrong decision or wrong data.

|---|---|---:|---|---|

| `26-wbs-table.png`, MCP writes | **1. Visibility of system status** | **4** | `PLT-06` conflict has no UI; the user does not know that the data they are editing has gone stale. | Version/presence signal; conflict dialog with the newer server value. |
| `09-workspace-fields-options.png` | **2. Match between system and real world** | **2** | Category, Type, Phase are system vocabulary that easily overlaps in meaning in real PM language. | Inline examples and glossary; preview “used for roll-up / used for classification”. |

## C3. The AI experience through MCP

### Reliability

**Observation from the documents**
- `MCP-10` makes the client use the metrics computed by the platform instead of recomputing them. This is a very good decision.
- `MCP-11` + BR-34 require every action to have audit attribution.
- `MCP-14` requires idempotency/optimistic versions.
- `MCP-08` + BR-35 keep the governance decision in a prepare-only state.
- `08-profile-ai-access.png` already has a connection/activity affordance; `06-tenant-admin-audit.png` has MCP detail.

**Risks**
- An LLM can produce content that is syntactically valid but wrong in business intent.
- A write tool can be based on a stale snapshot.
- A client retry can duplicate a write.
- Prompt injection from a comment/file can try to force the LLM to call a tool outside the intent.
- An overly broad token scope turns a model/client error into a data error.

### Transparency

Each AI-prepared artifact/action should show:
- **Prepared by AI via `<client>`**, the user identity and a timestamp.
- Tool name/version.
- Data snapshot / “as of”.
- Evidence links to the project/WBS/risk/gate source.
- Assumptions and missing data.
- Diff: before → proposed after.
- Confidence is used only if it has clear semantics; do not turn confidence into an “approval likelihood”.

The audit log should prioritize metadata; do not store the whole prompt/raw content by default if it is not needed, because it may contain sensitive data. Retention/log content needs a policy of its own.

### User control

Proposed tool classification:

| Class | Example | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| **Read** | get project, metric, WBS | Runs directly according to permission. |
| **Append-only low risk** | journal note/comment | Can run directly; the activity is clearly AI-attributed; supports delete/undo according to policy. |
| **Reversible write** | update status/target/assignee | Version check + idempotency; an optional tenant policy requires preview/confirm. |
| **High-risk/governance** | approve gate, apply CR, baseline, delete, permission, token/admin | **Not executed through the LLM**; prepare only; the user confirms in the app per BR-35. |

### Risks when an LLM writes data

1. **Stale write:** require `recordVersion`; if it mismatches return a conflict, no auto-merge.
2. **Duplicate:** require `idempotencyKey`.
3. **Bulk blast radius:** limit the number of records per call and require an explicit scope.
4. **Prompt injection:** tool output/input validation; treat external content as data; do not let content change the policy/tool scope by itself.
5. **Token theft:** a PAT is shown only once, hashed at rest, expiry/revoke, workspace restriction; OAuth secrets encrypted.
6. **Permission drift:** check permission at the time of the tool call, not only at token issuance.
7. **Metric hallucination:** return only a server-computed metric + definition/version.

### How to present a decision prepared by AI

In `12-gate-review.png` or `32-change-requests.png`:
- Banner: **AI prepared: no decision has been made**.
- A summary of the proposal, evidence, missing evidence, assumptions.
- Diff / impacted items.
- Buttons for the person with permission: **Confirm**, **Edit before confirm**, **Reject draft**.
- The final rationale belongs to the person who confirms; if AI prefilled it, the label “AI-drafted, edited by…” must be kept.
- The Decision Log records both the preparer client and the human confirmer.

### Compatibility

The MCP 2026-07-28 spec is a good foundation, but the client ecosystem is not uniform. Q08 must become a real test matrix. The product copy should use: **“Connect supported/standards-compliant MCP clients; verified clients are listed here”** instead of the guarantee “every LLM application that supports MCP”.

---

## C4. Learnability

### Terms that are hard for newcomers

| Term | Why it is hard | Proposal |
|---|---|---|
| **WBS** | A non-PMO user may only understand a task list. | The first time it appears: “WBS: the source work structure of the project”; glossary + example. |
| **Category vs Type** | Both sound like a classification. | Category = grouping/non-counting per BR-24; Type = kind of work item. Show a side-by-side example. |
| **Baseline** | Easily understood as the “current plan”. | Tooltip: a committed snapshot; after the baseline, changes must go through a CR. Link the BR-04 behavior. |
| **Gate** | Can be understood as any approval. | “Gate = the decision to move stage”; show evidence/quorum. |
| **Waiver** | Domain/legal-like term. | “Exception allowing progress despite unmet evidence”; always reason/approver/expiry if the policy requires it. |
| **Lifecycle Framework** | Abstract for a new PM. | Diagram + sample “Discover → Plan → Execute → Close”. |
| **Deliverable Process Framework** | Easily confused with the lifecycle. | Copy: “recipe to generate WBS for one deliverable”, not a project stage. |
| **PIC / Reviewer / Approver** | The role semantics may differ between organizations. | Hover definition + workspace role mapping source. |
| **Focus** | A branded noun that does not describe the scope. | Subtitle “My work today & this week”; a clear global vs project scope. |
| **Declared vs Computed health** | There are two truth signals. | Explain formulas and required rationale when they diverge. |

### Proposed onboarding

1. **First-run role-based tour**, not a tour of the whole product.
2. **Sample project** read-only, using the same data model so that users can try drill-down.
3. **Workspace setup checklist** with progress.
4. **Inline definition** at the first occurrence of a domain term, not a tooltip everywhere.
5. **Metric explanation drawer**: formula, exclusions, data freshness, source items.
6. A **“Why is this locked?”** link when a baseline/gate/permission blocks an operation.
7. **Command/search help** for power users.
8. The Builder has its own tutorial and sandbox preview; do not cram it into the app-wide onboarding.

# 7. Questions to ask the client before settling the spec

The questions below should be answered in Discovery. For any question that maps to a D-xx, update §19 directly to avoid having two sources of decisions.

1. **Who is the first design partner, which kind of workspace do they belong to, and what are their three mandatory journeys?** If Creative Studio and Digital Products are both targets, which one decides 1A?
2. **D-01:** does the client accept defining 1A as a pilot vertical slice or still require all of the current foundation/execution modules?
3. **D-28:** is the expected level of isolation a shared database + tenant policy, a schema/database per tenant or a dedicated environment for some tiers? Who owns this technical decision?
4. **D-20:** what is the first region? Is there any tenant that requires data/backup/telemetry to be in a specific jurisdiction?
5. **D-03:** does the pilot need SAML, OIDC or both? Are password + MFA and magic link really needed right in 1A?
6. **D-02:** is an external client/user a launch use case or can it be moved after the internal pilot?
7. **D-29 / Q08:** which three MCP clients must be officially supported at launch? Which client uses OAuth, which client uses PAT?
8. **D-26:** actual concurrency: how many people on the same project, the same WBS, the same item? What P95 latency and availability does the buyer expect?
9. **D-24:** does the client accept the current §12 formulas for progress/overdue/delayed/workload? Is there any metric that must be weighted by effort instead of item count?
10. **GOV-03/GOV-09:** can a gate have several different approver/quorum groups? Are abstain/delegation/substitute approver needed in the MVP?
11. **D-23:** which default set of lifecycle/process templates must exist on launch day? Who is the owner of the template content?
12. **D-09:** which use case must the Builder solve that manual WBS + template clone do not solve well enough? What frequency of PM use of the Builder is expected?
13. **D-08:** when a CR is approved, does the PM always Apply manually or is there a type of change that is auto-applied? If manual, what are the SLA/escalation?
14. **D-13:** does the PDF need a signature, legal footer, watermark, version number or only a presentational export?
15. **D-15:** may a role override at the project level go beyond the workspace role? Is any segregation-of-duties mandatory?
16. **D-16:** which notifications are mandatory besides approval? Who configures the overdue reminder cadence?
17. **D-31:** does the procurement target require SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or both? Is the certification milestone a blocker for production? **[Needs verification]**
18. **Retention:** how long are project/audit/file/token logs kept? Do customers have custom retention per tenant? **[Needs verification]**
19. **Support access:** does the customer require approving each support session? Is there any tenant that forbids support access entirely?
20. **Migration:** does the pilot have data from Excel/Jira/Smartsheet/POC that needs importing? If so, which import is really P0?
21. **Source of truth:** if Jira/ADO is synced later, which fields are Metis-authoritative and which fields are externally authoritative?
22. **Financial/value data:** if M19 is P1, where does the P0 Cockpit get “investment/value” from and what level of reliability may be displayed?
23. **Capacity:** does the supply/demand data come from manual entry, CSV or an HR system in the pilot? Who is responsible for freshness?
24. **MVP/product model:** is there any design partner that really uses the MVP/feature/release hierarchy in 1A? If not, can M14 be feature-flagged?
25. **Mobile:** does D-19 expect responsive review/approval or full WBS editing on mobile?
26. **Commercial:** which pricing unit is easier for the client to accept: active user, managed project, workspace or tier/module? Do not settle on a number before the procurement interviews.
27. **Adoption:** does the client accept measuring median time-to-weekly-update, stale-project rate and PM weekly active usage as success criteria?
28. **AI data egress:** does the tenant admin need an allowlist/denylist of LLM clients or tools per workspace?
29. **AI audit:** is there a need to store the raw prompt/response, or only metadata/redacted tool parameters? How long is the retention? **[Needs verification]**
30. **Decision accountability:** when AI drafts the rationale and the user edits then confirms, does the Decision Log need to keep the original AI draft as well or only the final human-approved text?

## 8.2 Assumptions used in the review

1. BRD v4.1 is the preferred source when it differs from the POC/old BRD, as per §1.
2. `manifest.json` is the main traceability map between the wireframes and the requirements; a case where the UI has an affordance but the manifest does not map it is recorded as a **traceability gap**, and does not automatically lead to the conclusion that the feature does not exist.
3. A mid-fidelity wireframe does not represent a pixel-perfect implementation; the review does not deduct points because the typography/spacing is not final, it only rates the density/accessibility risk.
4. The action count in C1 is a comparative estimate, not usability telemetry.
5. The team/time estimate in A3 is a planning envelope for a greenfield SaaS with managed cloud services and component libraries; it is not a bid/commitment.
6. It is not assumed that production-grade reusable POC code is available. Q03 of §19/Open questions needs to confirm this.
7. It is not assumed that every design partner needs M14 MVP/Product Delivery; this feature should follow the workspace/pilot need.
8. The MCP inference cost is borne by the customer-owned LLM according to the context the user provided; Metis still bears the infrastructure/operations cost of the MCP endpoint.
9. “Conditional Go” means **investing in Discovery + spikes + validation**, not committing to all 156 P0 right away.
10. There is no conclusion on market share, competitor pricing or revenue opportunity because there is no source strong enough in the pack.

## 8.3 List of [Needs verification] points

1. **The current competing capabilities** of Planview, Planisware, ServiceNow SPM, Jira Align, Smartsheet, monday.com, Asana; the products change fast.
2. **Competitors' MCP availability/capability**: Asana, monday.com and ServiceNow have current official documentation, but the scope/tool/auth/package may change.
3. **Competitive pricing:** the report gives no figures; a procurement/vendor quote is needed if it is used for a business case.
4. **Market share / analyst ranking:** the report does not use it because there is no independent source suitable enough for the ICP of Metis.
5. **Obligations on privacy/data residency/cross-border transfer/retention** per jurisdiction and data type.
6. Which **SOC 2/ISO 27001** the buyer really requires, the scope and the time by which it must be reached.
7. The specific **Subprocessor/DPA/incident obligations** under the customer contract.
8. The specific **Accessibility conformance target** (for example which standard version/level is contractual) if it is put into acceptance/procurement.
9. The actual **MCP client compatibility** with protocol revision 2026-07-28, OAuth/DCR/PAT of the clients that the client chooses.
10. **ICP willingness-to-pay / willingness-to-switch**; the BRD has no market evidence yet.
11. **Pilot data quality/capacity source** and the effort to maintain freshness.
12. **Reusability of the POC code** for production; a code review of Q03 is needed.

8. **Model Context Protocol: 2026-07-28 specification release.** The official blog/spec describes a stateless protocol core, header-based routing/cacheable list results and authorization hardening.

# Final conclusion

**Invest in Discovery, and do not commit to building BRD v4.1 as it stands.** Metis has a foundation product worth trying: WBS single source, metric consistency, structured governance and permission-equivalent MCP. But to become a feasible enterprise product, the team must do less first, measure real adoption, lock the tenant/security decisions and turn the error/concurrency/data-freshness states into part of the spec rather than “polish later”.

The most important point of Discovery is not to confirm that “all 156 requirements are reasonable”. It must answer three harder questions:

1. **Will PMs be willing to use Metis as the place to update real work?**
2. **Do the Executive/PMO make better decisions thanks to the traceability from the portfolio down to the WBS?**
3. **Can Metis provide tighter governance + AI access while still being lighter than the existing enterprise suites?**

If these three questions have positive evidence after the pilot, **Go** for the expanded build. If not, adding modules will only increase cost without fixing the core product risk.
